Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 1) The normal menstrual cycle length is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: A normal menstrual cycle ranges from 21 to 35 days in reproductive-age women.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 2) Menorrhagia is defined as:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.option4: Excessive menstrual bleeding occurring at regular intervals
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Menorrhagia refers to heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding with a regular cycle.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 3) Polymenorrhea refers to:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.option4: Menstrual cycles occurring at intervals of less than 21 days
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Polymenorrhea is characterized by frequent menstrual cycles.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 4) Oligomenorrhea is defined as:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Oligomenorrhea describes infrequent menstruation.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 5) Amenorrhea is defined as:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Amenorrhea refers to the absence of menstrual periods.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 6) Primary amenorrhea is classically defined as absence of menstruation by:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.option3: 15 years in girls with normal secondary sexual characteristics
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.option4: 13 years regardless of secondary sexual characteristics
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Primary amenorrhea is evaluated if menarche has not occurred by age 15 in girls with normal pubertal development.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 7) The most common cause of secondary amenorrhea is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Pregnancy should always be excluded first in any woman with secondary amenorrhea.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 8) Dysmenorrhea is defined as:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Dysmenorrhea refers to pain associated with menstruation.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 9) The most common cause of primary dysmenorrhea is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Increased endometrial prostaglandin production causes uterine contractions and pain.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 10) The first-line treatment for primary dysmenorrhea is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: NSAIDs inhibit prostaglandin synthesis and are the first-line treatment.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 11) The most common cause of secondary dysmenorrhea is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Endometriosis is the leading cause of secondary dysmenorrhea.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 12) Abnormal uterine bleeding due to ovulatory dysfunction is classified by FIGO as:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: “O” in the PALM-COEIN classification represents ovulatory dysfunction.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 13) Which of the following belongs to the structural causes of abnormal uterine bleeding in the PALM-COEIN classification?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: PALM represents structural causes: Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, and Malignancy/hyperplasia.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 14) The most common cause of abnormal uterine bleeding in adolescents is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Immaturity of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis commonly causes anovulatory bleeding.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 15) The most common cause of abnormal uterine bleeding in reproductive-age women should always be excluded first by:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Pregnancy and pregnancy-related complications must always be excluded first.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 16) A 16-year-old girl presents with irregular heavy menstrual bleeding since menarche. Pregnancy test is negative and examination is normal. The most likely cause is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Immaturity of the HPO axis commonly results in irregular anovulatory bleeding during adolescence.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 17) A 28-year-old woman presents with secondary amenorrhea for 10 weeks. What is the first investigation?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Pregnancy is the commonest cause of secondary amenorrhea and must be excluded first.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 18) A 24-year-old woman complains of severe spasmodic lower abdominal pain beginning just before menstruation and improving after the first day. Pelvic examination is normal. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Typical cyclical pain with a normal pelvic examination suggests primary dysmenorrhea.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 19) A 35-year-old multiparous woman presents with progressively worsening dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and infertility. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: The triad of dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and infertility strongly suggests endometriosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 20) A woman with heavy regular menstrual bleeding is found to have multiple intramural fibroids on ultrasound. According to FIGO PALM-COEIN classification, this is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Leiomyoma is represented by “L” in the PALM-COEIN classification.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 21) The most common physiological cause of vaginal discharge is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Clear, non-offensive discharge commonly occurs during ovulation because of estrogen.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 22) The commonest cause of pathological vaginal discharge is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Bacterial vaginosis is the most common cause of abnormal vaginal discharge in reproductive-age women.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 23) A thin, homogeneous, gray vaginal discharge with a fishy odor is most suggestive of:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Bacterial vaginosis classically presents with a thin gray discharge and fishy odor.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 24) A woman presents with intense vulval itching and thick, curdy-white vaginal discharge. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Candida infection causes pruritus with thick, white “cottage cheese” discharge.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 25) A woman presents with frothy yellow-green vaginal discharge, vulval irritation, and a “strawberry cervix” on examination. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Trichomonas vaginalis causes frothy discharge and the characteristic strawberry cervix.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 26) The vaginal pH in bacterial vaginosis is typically:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Bacterial vaginosis raises the vaginal pH above 4.5 due to replacement of lactobacilli by anaerobic bacteria.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 27) The organism most commonly responsible for bacterial vaginosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Gardnerella vaginalis is the principal organism associated with bacterial vaginosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 28) The bedside test that produces a fishy odor after adding 10% KOH to vaginal discharge is called the:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: A positive whiff (amine) test is characteristic of bacterial vaginosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 29) The vaginal pH in vulvovaginal candidiasis is usually:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Vaginal pH usually remains normal in candidiasis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 30) The drug of choice for uncomplicated vulvovaginal candidiasis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: A single oral dose of fluconazole is effective for uncomplicated candidiasis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 31) The drug of choice for bacterial vaginosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Metronidazole is the standard first-line treatment.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 32) The treatment of choice for trichomoniasis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Oral metronidazole is highly effective against Trichomonas vaginalis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 33) In trichomoniasis, treatment should include:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Treating both partners reduces reinfection.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 34) The most common endocrine cause of secondary amenorrhea is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: After excluding pregnancy, hyperprolactinemia is an important endocrine cause of secondary amenorrhea.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 35) The most common cause of hyperprolactinemia is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Prolactinoma is the commonest pathological cause of hyperprolactinemia.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 36) A 22-year-old woman presents with secondary amenorrhea and milky nipple discharge. Pregnancy test is negative. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Amenorrhea with galactorrhea strongly suggests elevated prolactin levels.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 37) A woman presents with heavy menstrual bleeding, fatigue, and pallor. Pregnancy test is negative. Ultrasound demonstrates a submucosal fibroid. The cause of her abnormal uterine bleeding is classified as:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Leiomyoma is classified under the structural causes (PALM).

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 38) A 17-year-old girl has heavy irregular menstrual bleeding since menarche. Hemoglobin is 7 g/dL. Ultrasound is normal. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Adolescents commonly experience anovulatory bleeding because of an immature HPO axis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 39) A 32-year-old woman presents with progressively worsening dysmenorrhea and infertility. Laparoscopy shows chocolate cysts in both ovaries. The diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Ovarian endometriomas (“chocolate cysts”) are characteristic of endometriosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 40) A woman complains of profuse thin gray vaginal discharge with a fishy smell that becomes more noticeable after intercourse. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: The characteristic fishy odor after intercourse is typical of bacterial vaginosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 41) A woman presents with intense vulval itching and dyspareunia. Vaginal pH is normal. Microscopy demonstrates budding yeast and pseudohyphae. The diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Budding yeast with pseudohyphae confirms Candida infection.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 42) A woman has frothy yellow-green vaginal discharge and motile flagellated organisms are seen on wet mount microscopy. The diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Motile flagellates on wet mount are diagnostic of trichomoniasis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 43) A woman presents with amenorrhea, obesity, acne, and hirsutism. Pregnancy test is negative. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: PCOS commonly presents with oligo/amenorrhea and clinical hyperandrogenism.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 44) A woman develops secondary amenorrhea following postpartum hemorrhage and failure to lactate. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Pituitary infarction after severe postpartum hemorrhage causes hypopituitarism.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 45) A woman with secondary amenorrhea has elevated FSH and low estrogen levels. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: High FSH with hypoestrogenism indicates ovarian failure.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 46) A 30-year-old woman presents with postcoital bleeding and persistent offensive vaginal discharge. Which diagnosis should be excluded first?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Persistent offensive discharge with postcoital bleeding is suspicious for cervical cancer.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 47) A woman with abnormal uterine bleeding undergoes endometrial biopsy. Which patient has the strongest indication for biopsy?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Women aged ≥45 years with AUB should undergo endometrial sampling to exclude malignancy.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 48) A woman with severe dysmenorrhea unresponsive to NSAIDs is found to have nodularity of the uterosacral ligaments on pelvic examination. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Tender nodules along the uterosacral ligaments are a classic finding in endometriosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 49) A woman presents with amenorrhea after repeated uterine curettage. Pregnancy test is negative. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Intrauterine adhesions following curettage commonly cause secondary amenorrhea.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 50) A woman presents with chronic vaginal discharge. Speculum examination shows a retained tampon. The discharge is most likely:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Retained foreign bodies can cause persistent foul-smelling vaginal discharge due to secondary infection.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 51) The most common cause of primary amenorrhea with normal secondary sexual characteristics is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: MRKH syndrome presents with primary amenorrhea, normal ovarian function, and normal secondary sexual characteristics.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 52) The most common cause of primary amenorrhea with absent secondary sexual characteristics is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Gonadal dysgenesis (Turner syndrome) is the leading cause of primary amenorrhea with delayed puberty.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 53) The most common chromosomal pattern in Turner syndrome is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Monosomy X (45,X) is the classical karyotype of Turner syndrome.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 54) The most common cause of cryptomenorrhea is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Imperforate hymen obstructs menstrual flow, causing cryptomenorrhea.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 55) The gold standard investigation for diagnosing endometriosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Laparoscopy allows direct visualization and histological confirmation of endometriosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 56) The most common symptom of endometriosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Progressive secondary dysmenorrhea is the commonest presenting symptom.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 57) According to the PALM-COEIN classification, adenomyosis belongs to:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Adenomyosis is a structural cause of abnormal uterine bleeding.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 58) The first-line imaging investigation for abnormal uterine bleeding due to suspected structural pathology is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: TVS is the preferred initial imaging modality for evaluating uterine pathology.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 59) The most common cause of postmenopausal bleeding is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Although carcinoma must be excluded, endometrial atrophy is the commonest cause.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 60) Postmenopausal bleeding should be considered:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.option2: Due to infection in most women
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Every case of postmenopausal bleeding requires evaluation to exclude malignancy.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 61) A 14-year-old girl has cyclical lower abdominal pain but has never menstruated. Examination reveals a bluish bulging membrane at the vaginal introitus. The diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Retained menstrual blood (hematocolpos) due to imperforate hymen causes cyclical pain.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 62) A 16-year-old girl has primary amenorrhea with normal breast development but absent uterus on ultrasound. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: MRKH syndrome presents with absent uterus but normal ovaries and secondary sexual characteristics.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 63) A woman presents with heavy menstrual bleeding. Pregnancy test is negative. Ultrasound demonstrates diffuse enlargement of the uterus without discrete fibroids. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Diffusely enlarged, tender uterus with heavy painful periods suggests adenomyosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 64) A 27-year-old woman presents with oligomenorrhea, obesity, acne, and infertility. Ultrasound shows enlarged ovaries with multiple peripheral follicles. The diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: These are classic clinical and ultrasound features of polycystic ovary syndrome.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 65) A woman with abnormal uterine bleeding is found to have an endometrial polyp. According to PALM-COEIN, this is classified as:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: “P” represents endometrial polyp.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 66) A woman complains of offensive frothy vaginal discharge. Wet mount demonstrates motile protozoa. Which associated cervical finding is most characteristic?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Punctate cervical hemorrhages produce the characteristic strawberry appearance.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 67) A woman with bacterial vaginosis undergoes microscopy. Which microscopic finding is most characteristic?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Vaginal epithelial cells coated with bacteria (“clue cells”) are diagnostic of bacterial vaginosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 68) A woman with vulvovaginal candidiasis is most likely to have which predisposing condition?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Diabetes, pregnancy, antibiotics, and immunosuppression predispose to Candida infection.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 69) A woman presents with recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis despite treatment. Which underlying condition should be actively excluded?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Poorly controlled diabetes is a common cause of recurrent candidiasis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 70) A woman complains of postcoital bleeding. Speculum examination reveals a friable cervical growth. The priority investigation is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: A suspicious cervical lesion requires biopsy to exclude cervical carcinoma.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 71) A 48-year-old woman presents with heavy irregular menstrual bleeding. Pregnancy test is negative. The most appropriate next investigation to exclude endometrial malignancy is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Women aged ≥45 years with abnormal uterine bleeding should undergo endometrial sampling.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 72) A 25-year-old woman has amenorrhea for 6 months. Pregnancy test is negative, prolactin and thyroid function tests are normal. The next appropriate step in evaluation is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: After excluding pregnancy, thyroid disease, and hyperprolactinemia, the progesterone challenge test helps assess estrogen status and outflow tract patency.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 73) A woman with secondary dysmenorrhea experiences deep dyspareunia, infertility, and dyschezia. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: The combination of dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, infertility, and dyschezia is highly suggestive of endometriosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 74) A postmenopausal woman presents with vaginal bleeding. Transvaginal ultrasound shows an endometrial thickness of 12 mm. The next step is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Thickened endometrium in postmenopausal bleeding requires histological evaluation.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 75) A woman presents with recurrent offensive vaginal discharge despite repeated empirical treatment. Speculum examination reveals a retained contraceptive sponge. The definitive management is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Persistent discharge due to a retained foreign body resolves after removal, with antibiotics if secondary infection is present.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 76) The most common cause of postmenopausal bleeding that must always be excluded is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Although endometrial atrophy is the commonest cause overall, postmenopausal bleeding should always be considered due to endometrial carcinoma until proven otherwise.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 77) The most common structural cause of abnormal uterine bleeding in reproductive-age women is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Uterine fibroids (leiomyomas) are the commonest structural cause of AUB.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 78) Ovulatory dysfunction causing abnormal uterine bleeding is classified under:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: COEIN includes non-structural causes: Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, and Not yet classified.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 79) The investigation of choice for confirming ovulation is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: A raised mid-luteal progesterone level confirms ovulation.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 80) The first-line medical treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding in women without structural pathology who also desire contraception is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: LNG-IUS is the most effective long-term medical treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 81) A 13-year-old girl presents with cyclical lower abdominal pain and primary amenorrhea. Examination reveals a bluish bulging hymen. The diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Obstruction of menstrual outflow results in hematocolpos and cyclical pain.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 82) A 17-year-old girl has primary amenorrhea. She has short stature, webbed neck, and shield chest. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: These are classic phenotypic features of Turner syndrome.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 83) A 26-year-old woman complains of amenorrhea for 8 months after severe postpartum hemorrhage. She is unable to breastfeed. Which hormone is expected to be low?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Sheehan syndrome causes pituitary insufficiency, resulting in low prolactin and failure of lactation.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 84) A woman with infertility has severe dysmenorrhea and dyspareunia. Laparoscopy reveals powder-burn lesions over the pelvic peritoneum. The diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Powder-burn lesions are characteristic laparoscopic findings in endometriosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 85) A 42-year-old woman presents with heavy regular menstrual bleeding. Pelvic examination reveals an enlarged irregular uterus. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: An enlarged irregular uterus with menorrhagia is typical of uterine leiomyomas.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 86) A woman presents with thin gray vaginal discharge. Vaginal pH is 5.5, the whiff test is positive, and clue cells are present. The diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Elevated vaginal pH, positive whiff test, and clue cells fulfill the diagnostic features of bacterial vaginosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 87) A pregnant woman presents with vulval itching and thick curdy-white vaginal discharge. The safest first-line treatment is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Topical azole antifungals are preferred for vulvovaginal candidiasis during pregnancy.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 88) A woman with frothy yellow-green vaginal discharge is diagnosed with trichomoniasis. Which additional sexually transmitted infection should routinely be screened for?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Trichomoniasis is associated with other STIs; patients should be screened appropriately, including for HIV.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 89) A woman presents with heavy menstrual bleeding and petechiae since adolescence. Pregnancy test is negative and pelvic ultrasound is normal. The most likely underlying cause is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Heavy bleeding from menarche with bleeding manifestations suggests an inherited bleeding disorder, especially von Willebrand disease.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 90) A 46-year-old obese woman presents with irregular heavy menstrual bleeding. She has diabetes and hypertension. Which diagnosis should be excluded first?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Obesity, diabetes, age >45 years, and abnormal uterine bleeding are important risk factors for endometrial carcinoma.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 91) A woman with secondary amenorrhea has a positive progesterone withdrawal test. This indicates:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.option1: Adequate estrogen production with a patent outflow tract
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Withdrawal bleeding indicates sufficient estrogen to stimulate the endometrium and an intact genital outflow tract.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 92) A woman presents with severe dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia, and a uniformly enlarged tender uterus. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Adenomyosis classically causes a boggy, enlarged, tender uterus with heavy painful periods.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 93) A woman with recurrent bacterial vaginosis asks about the likely complication during pregnancy. Which is the most important?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Bacterial vaginosis is associated with preterm labor, preterm rupture of membranes, and other adverse pregnancy outcomes.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 94) A woman with persistent galactorrhea and amenorrhea has markedly elevated prolactin levels. MRI demonstrates a pituitary microadenoma. The preferred initial treatment is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Dopamine agonists such as cabergoline are first-line therapy for prolactinomas.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 95) A 19-year-old woman has severe primary dysmenorrhea despite NSAID therapy and does not desire pregnancy. The next appropriate medical treatment is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Combined oral contraceptives suppress ovulation and reduce prostaglandin production, improving primary dysmenorrhea.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 96) A woman with postmenopausal bleeding undergoes transvaginal ultrasound showing an endometrial thickness of 3 mm. She has no further bleeding. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: A thin endometrium (<4 mm) in postmenopausal bleeding strongly suggests endometrial atrophy.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 97) A woman presents with abnormal uterine bleeding due to a large submucosal fibroid distorting the uterine cavity. According to the PALM-COEIN system, this is classified as:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Leiomyoma is categorized under the structural (PALM) causes of abnormal uterine bleeding.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 98) A woman complains of chronic vaginal discharge and contact bleeding. On examination, an ulcerative cervical lesion is noted. The definitive investigation is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Histopathological examination of a cervical biopsy confirms the diagnosis of cervical carcinoma.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 99) A woman presents with heavy menstrual bleeding and severe anemia. She is hemodynamically stable, and pregnancy has been excluded. What is the most appropriate initial step?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.option1: Stabilize anemia and evaluate the cause of bleeding
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Initial management includes assessment of hemodynamic status, correction of anemia, and investigation of the underlying cause.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 100) A 24-year-old woman presents with amenorrhea, hirsutism, obesity, acne, and infertility. Laboratory tests show an elevated LH:FSH ratio. The most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: PCOS is characterized by chronic anovulation, hyperandrogenism, and frequently an elevated LH:FSH ratio.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 101) The most common cause of secondary amenorrhea after excluding pregnancy is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: After pregnancy is excluded, PCOS is the commonest cause of secondary amenorrhea in reproductive-age women.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 102) The most common cause of postcoital bleeding in reproductive-age women that must be excluded is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Although benign conditions are common, cervical malignancy must always be excluded in women with postcoital bleeding.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 103) A 30-year-old woman presents with chronic pelvic pain, infertility, dysmenorrhea, and dyspareunia. Laparoscopy reveals multiple bluish-black implants over the ovaries and uterosacral ligaments. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Bluish-black (“powder-burn”) implants seen on laparoscopy are classic for endometriosis.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 104) A 47-year-old obese woman with diabetes presents with irregular heavy uterine bleeding. Pregnancy test is negative. Which investigation is most important to exclude malignancy?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Women aged ≥45 years or with risk factors for endometrial cancer require endometrial sampling.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 105) A 25-year-old woman presents with secondary amenorrhea. Pregnancy test is negative, TSH and prolactin levels are normal. She has no withdrawal bleeding after a progesterone challenge test. The next appropriate investigation is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Absence of withdrawal bleeding suggests hypoestrogenism or outflow tract obstruction; an estrogen-progesterone challenge helps differentiate these causes.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 106) A woman with abnormal uterine bleeding is diagnosed with von Willebrand disease. According to the PALM-COEIN classification, this is categorized as:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Coagulopathy (“C”) is one of the non-structural causes of abnormal uterine bleeding.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 107) A woman presents with persistent frothy vaginal discharge. Wet mount confirms Trichomonas vaginalis. Which counseling point is most important?
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.option2: Treat all sexual partners simultaneously and avoid intercourse until treatment is completed
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Simultaneous treatment of partners prevents reinfection and further transmission.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 108) A 34-year-old woman presents with menorrhagia and an enlarged irregular uterus. Ultrasound shows multiple intramural fibroids, the largest measuring 8 cm. She has completed her family and desires definitive treatment. The most appropriate management is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Hysterectomy is the definitive treatment for symptomatic fibroids in women who have completed childbearing.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 109) A 15-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea, cyclical pelvic pain, and urinary retention. Examination reveals a tense bluish hymenal membrane. The diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: Obstructed menstrual outflow causes accumulation of blood in the vagina, producing hematocolpos and occasionally urinary retention.

Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.question: 110) A 29-year-old woman presents with heavy menstrual bleeding. Pregnancy has been excluded, and transvaginal ultrasound is normal. Laboratory evaluation reveals no coagulopathy. She desires future fertility. According to the FIGO PALM-COEIN system, the most likely diagnosis is:
Menstrual Disorders & Vaginal Discharge.exp: In the absence of structural pathology or coagulopathy, ovulatory dysfunction is a common cause of abnormal uterine bleeding in reproductive-age women.
